properties.name: Yongbyon nuclear complex
properties.note: The heart of the nuclear program: reactors that make plutonium, a reprocessing plant and a uranium enrichment hall.

properties.name: Kangson enrichment site
properties.note: Suspected covert uranium enrichment plant near Pyongyang. Kim Jong Un visited an enrichment facility in 2024 in a rare public photo-op.

properties.name: Punggye-ri nuclear test site
properties.note: All six nuclear tests (2006-2017) happened here. Tunnels were blown up for cameras in 2018, then repaired.

properties.name: Pyongsan uranium mill
properties.note: Mines and processes uranium ore into yellowcake, the raw material for the enrichment program.

properties.name: Sohae Satellite Launching Station
properties.note: Main space launch site, also used for rocket engine tests. Launched the Malligyong-1 spy satellite in 2023.

properties.name: Tonghae Satellite Launching Ground
properties.note: East coast launch site used for early long-range rocket tests (1998, 2006, 2009).

properties.name: Sinpo shipyard
properties.note: Submarine base and shipyard where submarine-launched ballistic missiles (Pukguksong) are built and tested.

properties.name: Kusong testing ground
properties.note: Inland missile test area used for Hwasong-12 and other launches.

properties.name: Sunan (Pyongyang airport)
properties.note: Pyongyang’s international airport doubles as an ICBM launch pad. Several Hwasong-15 and -17 shots were fired from here.

properties.name: Kumsusan Palace of the Sun
properties.note: Mausoleum where the embalmed bodies of Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il lie in state.

properties.name: Kim Il Sung Square
properties.note: Site of the military parades where new missiles are often shown for the first time.

properties.name: Ryugyong Hotel
properties.note: 105-story pyramid started in 1987 and still not open. A symbol of the regime’s priorities.

properties.name: Hyesan
properties.note: Border city on the Yalu, across from China’s Changbai. Historically a major smuggling and crossing point, now heavily fenced.

properties.name: Musan
properties.note: Mining county on the Tumen River, a common crossing area. Several well-known escapees came from here.

properties.name: Hoeryong
properties.note: Border city on the Tumen. The river is narrow here, so it was a frequent crossing point before new fences went up after 2020.

properties.name: Sinuiju–Dandong bridge
properties.note: The Friendship Bridge over the Yalu. Most legal trade with China goes through here, and so does a lot of smuggled media.

properties.name: Panmunjom (Joint Security Area)
properties.note: The truce village in the DMZ. A soldier escaped across it under fire in 2017.

properties.name: Musan iron mine
properties.note: One of the largest open-pit iron mines in Asia. Ore exports to China were a big source of hard currency before sanctions.

properties.name: Kaesong Industrial Region
properties.note: Joint zone where South Korean companies employed over 50,000 North Korean workers. Shut down in 2016. The North blew up the nearby liaison office in 2020.

properties.name: Wonsan-Kalma resort
properties.note: Beach resort Kim Jong Un pushed for years, opened in 2025 mostly for Russian tourists. Also near a common missile launch area.

properties.name: Rason special economic zone
properties.note: Free trade zone where North Korea borders both China and Russia. The rail and road link to Russia runs through here.
